name: RockYou
significanceNote: Pivotal breach whose leaked wordlist ('rockyou.txt') became an industry standard benchmark for password cracking tools.

name: Sony PlayStation Network
significanceNote: Forced a 23-day outage and highlighted widespread vulnerability in corporate credential storage practices.

name: Dropbox
significanceNote: Demonstrated the resilience of memory-hard bcrypt hashing against offline brute-force cracking attempts.

name: LinkedIn
significanceNote: Unsalted hashes allowed attackers to crack 90%+ of credentials rapidly using pre-computed rainbow tables.

name: Adobe Systems
significanceNote: Reused ECB mode encryption revealed identical ciphertext blocks across matching user passwords.

name: Yahoo (3 Billion Breach)
significanceNote: The largest credential breach in internet history, affecting every user account registered on Yahoo.

name: Target Retail
significanceNote: Showcased third-party HVAC vendor credential compromise leading to widespread enterprise network infiltration.

name: eBay
significanceNote: Forced a global mandatory password reset across all 145M active users.

name: Ashley Madison
significanceNote: Flawed implementation exposing MD5 tokens allowed bypass of the primary bcrypt password protections.

name: Myspace
significanceNote: Truncated password hashes severely limited entropy and simplified dictionary rainbow table lookups.

name: Equifax
significanceNote: Unpatched web framework vulnerability led to massive PII and financial record exposure.

name: Marriott Starwood
significanceNote: Protracted 4-year unauthorized access highlighting long-term stealth persistence in enterprise infrastructure.

name: Canva
significanceNote: Demonstrated that proper bcrypt hashing prevents mass password cracking even when database tables leak.

name: Zynga
significanceNote: Large-scale breach affecting mobile gaming accounts, driving wider adoption of multi-factor authentication (MFA).

name: SolarWinds Supply Chain
significanceNote: Tampered software updates compromised government agencies and Fortune 500 enterprises worldwide.

name: T-Mobile
significanceNote: High-risk telecom breach enabling targeted SIM-swapping and 2FA bypass attacks.

name: Twitter (X)
significanceNote: API rate-limiting bypass allowed scraping of public handles linked to private email addresses.

name: LastPass Vault Leak
significanceNote: Exposed encrypted vault blobs to offline brute-forcing, reinforcing the need for high iteration counts and strong master passphrases.
